entries.title: Fall 2026: first day of classes
entries.content: The first day of instruction for Fall 2026 is Monday, August 24, 2026. Late registration (with a $25 late registration fee) begins the same day.

entries.title: Fall 2026: last day to add a course online
entries.content: Sunday, August 30, 2026 is the last day to add a Fall 2026 course online. Courses added after that need the appropriate signatures (the final day to add with signatures is Friday, December 11, 2026).

entries.title: Fall 2026: withdraw from the term with a full refund
entries.content: Sunday, August 30, 2026 is the Fall 2026 deadline to withdraw from the whole term with a full refund (less the term withdrawal fee).

entries.title: Labor Day 2026 (university holiday)
entries.content: Labor Day, Monday, September 7, 2026, is an all-university holiday at WSU.

entries.title: Fall 2026: deadline to switch to pass/fail or audit
entries.content: Friday, September 11, 2026 is the last day in Fall 2026 to change a course from letter-graded to pass/fail, or between credit and audit. Changing from pass/fail back to letter-graded is allowed until Friday, December 11, 2026.

entries.title: Fall 2026: last day to drop a course without record
entries.content: The Fall 2026 deadline to drop a course without a record is Tuesday, September 22, 2026. After that, course withdrawals show on your transcript. Undergraduate and professional students can still withdraw from a course until Friday, November 20, 2026 (withdrawals don't reduce tuition). For late withdrawal options, contact the Office of the Registrar.

entries.title: Fall 2026: apply to graduate without a late fee
entries.content: Friday, October 2, 2026 is the last day to apply for a Fall 2026 undergraduate or professional degree or certificate without a late fee. After that a $75 late fee applies, rising to $150 after Friday, December 11, 2026. Graduate degree applications are also due October 2.

entries.title: Priority registration for Spring 2027
entries.content: Priority registration for Spring 2027 courses begins Monday, November 9, 2026.

entries.title: Veterans Day 2026 (university holiday)
entries.content: Veterans Day, Wednesday, November 11, 2026, is an all-university holiday at WSU.

entries.title: Fall 2026: last day to withdraw from a course
entries.content: Friday, November 20, 2026 is the Fall 2026 deadline for undergraduate and professional students to withdraw from a course (see Rule 68). Withdrawals are recorded on your transcript and don't reduce tuition charges. The deadline to withdraw from the whole term is Friday, December 11, 2026 (Rule 70b).

entries.title: Fall 2026 Thanksgiving break
entries.content: Thanksgiving vacation for Fall 2026 runs Monday, November 23 through Friday, November 27, 2026.

entries.title: Fall 2026: last day of classes
entries.content: Friday, December 11, 2026 is the last day of instruction for Fall 2026. It's also the deadline to withdraw from the whole term, to change from pass/fail back to letter-graded, and to add a course with the appropriate signatures.

entries.title: Fall 2026 commencement (graduation ceremony)
entries.content: Fall 2026 commencement for the Pullman campus is Saturday, December 12, 2026.

entries.title: Fall 2026 final exams week
entries.content: Fall 2026 final examinations run Monday, December 14 through Friday, December 18, 2026. Final grades are available in myWSU on Wednesday, December 23, 2026.

entries.title: Spring 2027: first day of classes
entries.content: The first day of instruction for Spring 2027 is Monday, January 11, 2027. Late registration (with a $25 late registration fee) begins the same day, and the last day to add a course online is Sunday, January 17, 2027.

entries.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Day 2027 (university holiday)
entries.content: Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Monday, January 18, 2027, is an all-university holiday at WSU.

entries.title: Spring 2027: last day to drop a course without record
entries.content: The Spring 2027 deadline to drop a course without a record is Tuesday, February 9, 2027. After that, course withdrawals show on your transcript. Undergraduate and professional students can withdraw from a course until Friday, April 16, 2027.

entries.title: Spring 2027 spring break
entries.content: Spring vacation for 2027 runs Monday, March 15 through Friday, March 19, 2027.

entries.title: Spring 2027: last day to withdraw from a course
entries.content: Friday, April 16, 2027 is the Spring 2027 deadline for undergraduate and professional students to withdraw from a course (see Rule 68). Withdrawals don't reduce tuition charges. The deadline to withdraw from the whole term is Friday, April 30, 2027.

entries.title: Spring 2027 final exams week
entries.content: Spring 2027 final examinations run Monday, May 3 through Friday, May 7, 2027. The last day of classes is Friday, April 30, 2027.

entries.title: Spring 2027 commencement (graduation ceremony)
entries.content: Spring 2027 commencement for the Pullman campus is Saturday, May 8, 2027. Other campuses: Tri-Cities on Sunday, May 9; Vancouver on Wednesday, May 12; Everett on Friday, May 14; and Global Campus on Saturday, May 15, 2027.

entries.title: Fall 2026 Family Weekend
entries.content: Fall 2026 Family Weekend at WSU Pullman is Friday, October 2 through Sunday, October 4, 2026. Highlights include comedian Dusty Slay at Beasley Coliseum (Friday, Oct. 2 at 7 p.m.), Cougar Football vs. Fresno State (Saturday, Oct. 3 at 6:30 p.m.), women's volleyball vs. San Diego State (Saturday, Oct. 3), and women's soccer vs. Fresno State (Sunday, Oct. 4). No formal RSVP is required.

entries.title: Spring 2027 Family Weekend
entries.content: Spring 2027 Family Weekend at WSU Pullman is Friday, April 2 through Sunday, April 4, 2027.

Ask me whether a specific spot is open right now!

entries.title: Holland and Terrell Libraries
entries.content: Holland and Terrell Libraries are on the WSU Pullman campus. Reference Services: 509-335-8516 or lib.reference@wsu.edu. Access Services: 509-335-9672. These are the regular fall 2026 hours; they change during breaks and finals, so check the Libraries' hours page for the latest.

entries.content: Owen Science and Engineering Library is on the WSU Pullman campus (phone 509-335-2672). These are the regular fall 2026 hours (closed on weekends); check the Libraries' hours page for the latest.

entries.title: Student Recreation Center (SRC)
entries.content: The Student Recreation Center is the largest recreation space on the WSU Pullman campus. Contact University Recreation at 509-335-8732 (509-335-UREC) or urec@wsu.edu. These are the regular fall 2026 building hours; check UREC's hours page for changes.

entries.title: SRC Pool
entries.content: The SRC Pool is in the Student Recreation Center. On weekdays it's open in three blocks (early morning, midday, and evening). These are the regular fall 2026 hours; check UREC's hours page for changes.

entries.title: Student Recreation Center amenities
entries.content: The Student Recreation Center (SRC) is the largest recreation space on the WSU Pullman campus. It has basketball, volleyball, badminton, pickleball, racquetball, and squash courts; weight and cardio equipment; fitness classes and personal training; a pool and spa; a 1/8-mile running track; a climbing and bouldering wall; a challenge course; a sport court for soccer and inline hockey; plus billiards, lockers, and towel service. WSU students, faculty, and staff sign in with their WSU Network ID to manage memberships, lockers, and registrations.

entries.title: Getting your CougarCard (student ID)
entries.content: To get your CougarCard (WSU's ID card), visit the CougarCard Center in person. At WSU Pullman it's in the Compton Union Building (CUB), room G60. Bring a valid photo ID: a driver's license, state ID card, military ID, passport, or Residence Alien Card. Your photo is taken on the spot and you get your card right away. Questions: cougarcard@wsu.edu or 509-335-2273.

entries.title: Office of the Registrar
entries.content: The Office of the Registrar handles registration, enrollment records, transcripts, residency, graduation applications, and withdrawals. It's in the French Administration Building, Room 346 (1815 NE Wilson Road, Pullman). Phone 509-335-5346 or email registrar@wsu.edu.

entries.title: WSU Pullman admission dates and deadlines (2026-27)
entries.content: Key WSU Pullman admission dates for the 2026-27 cycle: applications and the WSU General Scholarship application open August 3. The FAFSA and WASFA are scheduled to open October 1. November 15 is the priority date for spring admission. The summer and fall housing application opens December 1. January 31 is the priority date for the WSU General Scholarship and for the FAFSA/WASFA, and the Top Scholar consideration deadline. March 31 is the fall priority date for first-year applicants: apply by then to be considered for automatic academic awards (later applications are accepted as space allows). Confirm your enrollment and submit your housing application by May 1 for priority. Financial aid verification documents (if required) are due July 31. For transfer students, the priority date is August 7.

entries.title: Campus life and student organizations
entries.content: WSU Pullman has 500+ student organizations, from sports and gaming to cultural, academic, and media groups, plus a Greek system of 50+ chapters with nearly 3,500 members (about 22% of students). Find clubs on WSU Involve: open the Organizations tab, browse by category, and check meeting times and contacts. There are also 80+ intramural sports activities, free movies at the CUB, big-name shows at Beasley Coliseum, and Cougar athletics across 11 sports. Popular spots include the Compton Union Building (CUB), the Student Recreation Center, the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art, and the Elson S. Floyd Cultural Center.

entries.title: WSU Cougars athletics
entries.content: WSU's teams are the Cougars (the Cougs), competing at the NCAA Division I level in the Pac-12 Conference. Sports include football, volleyball, soccer, basketball, tennis, baseball, and more. Football plays at Gesa Field in Martin Stadium, and men's basketball plays in Beasley Coliseum.

entries.title: 2026 Cougar football home games
entries.content: Cougar football home games in 2026 are at Gesa Field in Martin Stadium, Pullman: Duquesne (Sat, Sept 19), Arizona (Sat, Sept 26), Fresno State (Sat, Oct 3), Boise State (Sat, Oct 24), Colorado State (Sat, Nov 14), and Oregon State (Sat, Nov 28). The Pac-12 Football Championship is Friday, December 4.

entries.title: 2026 Apple Cup (WSU vs. Washington)
entries.content: The Apple Cup is WSU's rivalry game against the University of Washington. In 2026 it was played Sunday, September 6 at Husky Stadium in Seattle.

entries.title: Student Sports Pass (student tickets)
entries.content: The 2026-27 Student Sports Pass costs $299 for Pullman students ($200 for urban and online campus students). It gets you into all regular-season home events in football, soccer, volleyball, men's and women's basketball, and baseball from August through May. Buy it in myWSU (Student Homepage, Manage Classes, Optional Services). The pass is digital: log in at wsucougars.com/MyAccount, add "My Access Pass" to Apple or Google Wallet, and scan it at the Student Entrance. Student sections are first come, first served and can fill up. Refund requests for an unused pass are due November 13, 2026.

entries.title: 2026-27 men's basketball home games
entries.content: Cougar men's basketball plays at Beasley Coliseum in Pullman. The first home games of the 2026-27 season are Davidson (Monday, November 2), Idaho (Friday, November 27), and North Dakota State (Sunday, December 6). Tip-off times are still to be announced.

entries.title: Game day traditions and the ZZU Cru
entries.content: The ZZU Cru is the official student fan club of the Cougs and drives the energy at WSU athletic events. Cougar football game days in Pullman are a town-wide celebration with tailgating near Martin Stadium, and the Cougar Marching Band supports the teams and plays the fight song.

entries.title: Getting started in undergraduate research
entries.content: WSU's Office of Undergraduate Research helps undergrads get into research, scholarship, and creative work. Good first steps: take UNIV 199, a one-credit "Introduction to Directed Research" course offered fall and spring; book a chat with a peer mentor (current undergrad researchers); go to the STEM Research Opportunities Fair and info sessions; and reach out to faculty in your department about joining their work. Support programs include LSAMP, the McNair Scholars Program, Research Scholars (for incoming first-year students), and the Team Mentoring Program. Some courses also build research right into the class.

links.label: Office of Undergraduate Research: Get Started

entries.title: Undergraduate Research Awards (2027-28 funding)
entries.content: The Office of Undergraduate Research funds Undergraduate Research Awards for all WSU undergrads doing research, scholarship, or creative activities with a mentor. Applications for awards paid in the 2027-28 academic year open Monday, November 2, 2026 and close January 31, 2027. The office also offers travel awards to help students present at conferences.

entries.title: SURCA 2027 (undergraduate research showcase)
entries.content: SURCA, the Showcase for Undergraduate Research and Creative Activities, is WSU's annual poster showcase where around 200 undergrads present their work and compete for awards. SURCA 2027 is Monday, March 22, 2027: public presentations run 3:30-4:45 p.m. in the CUB Senior Ballroom, and the awards ceremony starts at 5 p.m. in the CUB Auditorium.

entries.title: Cougar Health Services
entries.content: Cougar Health Services, in the Washington Building, is WSU Pullman's student health center: primary care, counseling (CAPS), vision care, pharmacy, reproductive care, sports medicine, LGBTQ+ care, and psychiatry. Services run 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays (the pharmacy opens at 9:00 AM) and are closed on weekends and university holidays. Book medical and vision visits in the patient portal at healthweb.wsu.edu, or call 509-335-3575. In an emergency, call 911.

entries.title: Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS)
entries.content: CAPS, part of Cougar Health Services in the Washington Building, offers brief individual and couples therapy, group counseling, psychological assessment, biofeedback, and psychiatric services. New students schedule an initial consultation with the Make an Appointment button on the CAPS site, or call 509-335-4511 during business hours. After hours, call 509-335-2159. If you're in danger or it's an emergency, call 911.

entries.title: WSU housing (residence halls and apartments)
entries.content: WSU Housing and Residence Life runs the residence halls and campus apartments in Pullman, including Learning Living Communities and Gender Inclusive Housing. Apply online through the housing site ("Apply for a Residence Hall" or "Apply for an Apartment"). Questions? Call (509) 335-4577, email housing@wsu.edu, or stop by Streit-Perham Hall, 2nd floor.

entries.title: Free peer tutoring (ASCC)
entries.content: ASCC Peer Tutoring is free for WSU students in subjects like biology, chemistry, accounting, business, computer science, engineering, economics, physics, statistics, and psychology. Book a one-on-one appointment in the tutoring portal (log in, then "Book Me"), or just drop in: Lighty Student Services Room 190 (appointments Mon-Thu 1-5 pm), Streit-Perham Hall and Stephenson Hall (drop-in Sun-Thu 5-8 pm), and Terrell Library (drop-in and appointments Mon-Wed 5-8 pm). Contact (509) 335-6000 or ascc@wsu.edu.

entries.title: Career coaching (ASCC)
entries.content: Career coaches at the Academic Success and Career Center (ASCC) help you explore majors and careers, polish your resume and cover letter, prep for interviews, network, and find internships and jobs. Book in Handshake (Career Center, Appointments, Schedule a New Appointment, then "The Academic Success and Career Center - Pullman"), in person or virtual. ASCC is in Lighty Student Services, Rooms 160-190, open Monday-Friday 8:00 am-5:00 pm; call (509) 335-6000 or email ascc@wsu.edu.
